label: diabetic_retinopathy

ordering_verification.code_path: BRSETMultiLabel reads labels.csv and uses .iloc[idx]; test DataLoader shuffle=False; run_inference concatenates batches in order => npz row i == csv data row i
ordering_verification.residual_caveat: the value check alone cannot exclude a permutation that only swaps rows with an identical (DR, ME) label pair; the code path above is what excludes it
ordering_verification.also_identical: data/finetune_joint/test/labels.csv (the path the runs actually used) has byte-identical file/DR/ME columns in the same order, differing only by an extra `domain` column

caveats: Every arm, including the 'zero-shot' ones, tuned its decision threshold on the 725-image REAL mBRSET validation set. These arms are zero-shot in training data only, never in threshold selection.
42 is a count of IMAGES. 159 DR-positive images come from 59 patients; image false negatives are not patient misses.
The reported pooled headline 0.9463 / 0.8365 is the MEAN over the three joint seeds, not any single cached model; per-seed values are 0.9377/0.8250, 0.9519/0.8449, 0.9492/0.8396.
Noise floors used as the bar for calling anything an effect: DR AUC 0.0142, DR F1 0.0199.
No patient identifiers or filenames are written to this file; case references are row indices into the ordered 732-row test manifest.

s1_ranking_vs_calibration._question: How much of the zero-shot deficit is bad ordering (AUC) versus a badly placed threshold?

decomposition_f1.note: oracle_f1 is the ceiling of ANY monotone recalibration (Platt, temperature, isotonic): a monotone map cannot change the ranking, so it cannot beat the best cut point. Residual beyond that is representation, not calibration.

s2_which_cases._question: Which positives does the zero-shot model miss, who recovers them, and how big is the core nobody gets?
s2_which_cases._unit: IMAGES, not patients. 159 DR-positive images come from 59 patients; an image false negative is not a patient miss.

all_models._label: every run with a val-tuned threshold

hard_core_threshold_free._definition: per-positive AUC contribution c = fraction of the 573 negatives it outranks; max taken over ALL 732-row runs including ones without thresholds

patient_level._definition: a DR-positive patient is detected if ANY of their DR-positive images is predicted positive; identifiers replaced by anonymous ordinals

s3_score_distributions._question: Is the zero-shot model under-confident on positives (a shift a threshold could fix) or does it genuinely fail to separate them (overlap)?

pure_shift_ceiling.note: an additive logit shift is monotone, so its best F1 equals the oracle cut-point F1 reported here; any gap to pooled is overlap

auc_restricted._definition: positives split by the ZERO-SHOT model's per-positive AUC contribution (worst/best quartile), negatives kept whole

s4_real_vs_synthesis._question: If real target images recover a specific set and synthesis recovers none of it, what is that set like?

definitions.real_fix: detected by >=2 of 3 pooled (3402 real target) seeds
definitions.synth_fix: detected by >=1 of 4 synthesis arms (deliberately generous)

s4_real_vs_synthesis._quality_note: image appearance was already ruled out as the cause of the gap; these columns are here only so the recovered/unrecovered subsets can be checked against the whole-set means rather than read in isolation

s5_agreement._question: Are the synthesis arms making the baseline's errors plus extra ones, or different errors?

s6_ensemble._question: Does averaging zero-shot-eligible models clear the noise floor?
s6_ensemble._protocol_note: Picking the subset by TEST score is selection on the evaluation set and is reported only as an upper bound. The honest number is the subset chosen on VALIDATION.

s7_concentration._question: Is the pooled model's advantage concentrated in a few cases or spread evenly?
s7_concentration._identity: AUC == mean over positives of c_i, where c_i is the fraction of negatives that positive outranks. The AUC gap therefore splits exactly across positives.

n_positive_images_that_account_for_the_w.interpretation: the minimum number of positive images whose improved ranking alone reproduces the entire AUC gap; the rest of the positives net out to zero or negative

s8_cross_links._question: How do the hard core, the zero-shot misses and the concentrated-gain set relate, and what does the label budget curve look like?
s8_cross_links.interpretation_note: cases in the stable gain set but NOT in the zero-shot missed set are positives the zero-shot model already called correctly; the pooled model's AUC gain there is re-ranking headroom that never shows up in the false-negative count

hard_core_ranking_detail._reading: c = fraction of the 573 negatives this positive outranks. A hard-core case with max_c near 1 is ranked high by some model but still under every threshold, i.e. a threshold problem for that case; max_c near 0.5 means genuinely unseen by every model.
